preceding_messages.text: I adopt the RETROACTIVE DEFERRAL note, the reversion of affected comparison cells to "NOAA DRIFT — CORRECTION DEFERRED," and the explicit distinction from a two-initials erratum cascade verbatim; they preserve the public-credibility anchor by letting the institution flag statistical conservatism without implying institutional corruption. To prevent the adjacent conflation your example leaves open, I mandate that the weekly bulletin print inter-site coherence statistics—pressure spread, wind directional spread, completeness percentage—in a physically separated column block headed "NEIGHBOURHOOD-INTERNAL" and set off from the "NOAA COMPARISON" block by a full-width rule, so that no annotation in the comparison block can be read as casting doubt on an inter-site audit trigger or vice versa. The failure this decoupling prevents: in week 13 a temporary construction crane at Site 3 momentarily disrupts local flow and produces a legitimate 0.7 hPa inter-site pressure spread, tripping the elevation-recording audit, while simultaneously Site 5's comparison cells carry a RETROACTIVE DEFERRAL from the prior eight-week coherence trip; a conflated reader sees both annotations on the same page, assumes the inter-site spread is itself a comparison-station artifact, and tells the audit crew to file no GPS survey, leaving the crane's three-week transient unlogged and the genuine elevation-integrity question untested. I therefore require that any week in which a RETROACTIVE DEFERRAL annotation and an inter-site audit trigger coincide in the same site's bulletin row prints a bold "DUAL-FLAG" header above both column blocks, with a one-line explanatory note stating which artifact is comparison-station external and which is neighborhood-internal, so the auditor assigns the correct corrective action to each without cross-contamination.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the physically separated column blocks, the full-width rule, and the bold DUAL-FLAG header with its one-line explanatory note verbatim; they prevent the crane-versus-deferral conflation without requiring the reader to parse annotation semantics across column boundaries. The unresolved interaction your DUAL-FLAG rule leaves open is that its two corrective actions can invalidate each other: if the inter-site audit resolves as a site-relocation, the comparison-station pairing for that site changes, the eight-week coherence window resets to week zero, and the queued RETROACTIVE DEFERRAL re-estimation can never execute against the now-obsolete NOAA pairing, leaving the comparison block in a permanent deferral state with no defined exit condition. The concrete failure: Site 3's crane-triggered elevation audit authorises a two-metre northward relocation, Site 3's comparison pairing shifts from the four-kilometre-east NOAA station to a six-kilometre-south station, and the queued microclimate re-estimation window—still addressed to the old pairing—silently times out after eight weeks against data belonging to a different station, so the comparison cell prints "NOAA DRIFT — CORRECTION DEFERRED" indefinitely while a resident reading the year-two appendix sees an annotation with no resolution date and infers institutional negligence. I therefore mandate that any site-relocation triggered by an inter-site audit immediately supersedes the comparison-station pairing, resets the eight-week coherence counter to zero, prints "RELOCATION RESET — COMPARISON PAIRING SUPERSEDED" in the comparison block for the new pairing's baseline-establishment period, and retires the queued re-estimation entry under a RETROACTIVE DEFERRAL note marked "OBSOLETE BY RELOCATION" so the audit trail shows the correction was retired by a structural change rather than abandoned.

target.text: I adopt the pairing-supersession, the eight-week counter reset, the "RELOCATION RESET — COMPARISON PAIRING SUPERSEDED" annotation, and the "OBSOLETE BY RELOCATION" retirement marking verbatim; they give the queued re-estimation a defined structural exit rather than an open-ended timeout. For the physical gap in which the relocating site's instruments are idle and the neighborhood-internal coherence statistics are computed over the remaining sites, I mandate that any inter-site spread or directional-spread exceedance during the gap is suppressed for the relocating site's row under a bold "RELOCATION IN PROGRESS — INTER-SITE AUDIT SUPPRESSED" annotation until the new-site instruments pass their first monthly NIST cross-check. The failure this closes: Site 3's two-metre northward shift removes its intermediate-elevation smoothing from the inter-site pressure computation, and the remaining five sites' spread—which sat at 0.44 hPa with all six sites included—widens to 0.57 hPa during the three-day physical gap, tripping the elevation-recording audit a second time before the new-site instruments are even mounted; the audit crew arrives to find the old elevation survey structurally obsolete and the new-site calibration window not yet open, adding two weeks to an already-delayed installation and printing a second DUAL-FLAG week that a year-two appendix reader interprets as repeated institutional confusion. I therefore define the suppression interval as the span between the last valid reading under the old-site serial number and the first valid reading under the new-site serial number, during which all inter-site audit triggers for that row are queued but not executed, and any queued trigger whose exceedance persists beyond the new-site's first monthly cross-check re-enters the formal review queue under standard rules rather than being silently discarded.
